# Agent surface audit

<!-- Generated by scripts/agent-surface/audit.ts. Do not edit by hand; run `pnpm agent-surface:audit`. -->

This page measures what an agent meets when it drives GOAT today: the tools mounted on `/mcp` and the `goat` command tree. Every count and cited file comes from loading those registries from source (`scripts/agent-surface/inventory.ts`), so regenerating after a change shows whether a finding still holds. It is the evidence base for the agent surface redesign: it describes problems and ranks fixes, and leaves the target design to that spec.

Run `node scripts/agent-surface/inventory.ts` for the full JSON inventory, including per-tool schemas, hints, enforced access, and the rendered `--help` of every command.

## Naming

Tool names follow three shapes, so an agent cannot guess a name from the resource and verb it wants:

| Shape                | Count | Examples                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `resource_verb`      | 32    | `channel_bot_home`, `channel_bot_home_claim`, `channel_ingest`, `channel_input_get`, `channel_task_export`, `channel_task_get`, and 26 more                                       |
| `verb_resource`      | 38    | `create_threads`, `delegate_task`, `delete_scheduled_task`, `link_pull_request`, `list_scheduled_tasks`, `list_thread_pull_requests`, and 32 more                                 |
| `goat_resource_verb` | 132   | `goat_attachment_discard`, `goat_attachment_pending_list`, `goat_attachment_prepare_upload`, `goat_cloud_holders`, `goat_cloud_launch`, `goat_cloud_machine_create`, and 126 more |

The `goat_` prefix marks only some tools, and the catalog test pins exactly that set (apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/core.test.ts `publishes unique tool names`). `create_threads`, `delegate_task`, `delete_scheduled_task`, `link_pull_request`, `list_scheduled_tasks`, `list_thread_pull_requests`, `preview_back`, `preview_click`, and 30 more put the verb first, and `channel_bot_home`, `channel_bot_home_claim`, `channel_ingest`, `channel_input_get`, `channel_task_export`, `channel_task_get`, `channel_task_list`, `channel_task_move`, and 24 more put an unprefixed resource first. Pull requests use `link_pull_request` and `watch_pull_request` where threads use `goat_thread_watch`; scheduled tasks are `schedule_task`, `list_scheduled_tasks`, and `run_scheduled_task_now`.

## Schemas and envelopes

- **Undeclared arguments.** 182 of 202 published input schemas say `"additionalProperties": true`, but every registration refuses undeclared arguments at call time ((not found)). A client that validates against the schema cannot learn the real contract.
- **Two failure modes.** Tools split 161 `return` and 41 `error`. Both reach the client as `isError` with JSON in a text block and no `structuredContent` (apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/core.test.ts `declaredFailure`), so an agent parses text to branch on an error.
- **7 error families.** 160 tools fail with `OrchestratorMcpFailure`; 4 tools fail with 8 tagged errors; 3 tools fail with `OperationError`; 25 tools fail with 19 tagged errors; 1 tools fail with `OrchestratorMcpFailure` or `SshThreadHandoffFailure`; 2 tools fail with `OrchestratorMcpFailure` or `WorktreeMcpFailure`; 7 tools fail with 15 tagged errors. Only `OrchestratorMcpFailure` carries a machine `code` (packages/contracts/src/orchestratorMcpFailure.ts `OrchestratorMcpFailureCode`). Preview, device, worktree, and pull request failures are told apart by `_tag` alone, and every preview tool advertises all of its toolkit's tags whether or not it can raise them.
- **Idempotency.** 49 tools accept `clientRequestId`: `channel_bot_home_claim`, `channel_ingest`, `create_threads`, `delegate_task`, `device_open`, `goat_attachment_prepare_upload`, `goat_cloud_launch`, `goat_cloud_machine_create`, `goat_decision_request`, `goat_goal_apply`, and 39 more. The other 81 mutating tools have no retry key, including the destructive `delete_scheduled_task`, `device_close`, `goat_attachment_discard`, `goat_call`, `goat_cloud_run_forget`, `goat_connection_remove`, `goat_decision_answer`, `goat_environment_preferences_update`, `goat_goal_delete`, `goat_host_link_remove`, and 26 more.
- **Pagination.** 12 tools use `cursor/nextCursor` (`channel_task_export`, `channel_task_list`, `goat_cloud_run_list`, `goat_goal_list`, and 8 more); 9 tools use `limit only` (`goat_decision_list`, `goat_describe`, `goat_ssh_browse`, `goat_ssh_reports`, and 5 more); 1 tool uses `afterSequence/hasMore` (`goat_origin_reports_wait`); 1 tool uses `limit/hasMore` (`goat_thread_read`). List tools with no page control: `device_list`, `goat_attachment_pending_list`, `goat_cloud_machine_list`, `goat_connection_list`, `goat_host_link_list`, `goat_note_list`, `goat_pending_request_list`, `goat_provider_addable_list`, `goat_ssh_host_list`, `goat_thread_watch_list`, `list_scheduled_tasks`, `list_thread_pull_requests`.
- **Hints that disagree with enforcement.** The handler's `McpToolAccess` declaration is what the server enforces; the MCP `readOnlyHint` is what clients see. They disagree for no tools. Reads declared `actsAsCaller` without a read-only hint: `task_status`.
- **Image results.** `preview_snapshot`, `device_screenshot`, and `html_preview` are registered by hand to return image content (apps/server/src/mcp/McpHttpServer.ts `imageToolRegistration`), outside the toolkit path every other tool uses.

## Descriptions and examples

Only 21% of input parameters carry a description. 137 tools describe none of their parameters, for example `channel_bot_home_claim`, `channel_ingest`, `channel_input_get`, `channel_task_export`, `channel_task_get`, `channel_task_list`, `channel_task_move`, `channel_task_report`, `create_threads`, `delete_scheduled_task`, and 127 more. Optional fields encode as `anyOf [T, null]` with no stated default, so an agent learns defaults only from prose.

3 of 202 tool descriptions include an example. 100 tools have no `Tool.Title`. Description length is uneven; the longest are:

| Tool                     | Characters | Declared at                                             |
| ------------------------ | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `goat_ssh_thread_launch` | 399        | packages/contracts/src/agentSurface/entries/ssh.ts      |
| `delegate_task`          | 398        | packages/contracts/src/agentSurface/entries/task.ts     |
| `goat_describe`          | 393        | packages/contracts/src/agentSurface/surfaceEntries.ts   |
| `schedule_task`          | 383        | packages/contracts/src/agentSurface/entries/schedule.ts |
| `goat_thread_launch`     | 376        | packages/contracts/src/agentSurface/entries/thread.ts   |
| `goat_worktree_handoff`  | 364        | packages/contracts/src/agentSurface/entries/worktree.ts |

Long descriptions carry routing policy (when to use another tool, what to tell the user) that every session pays for in context and no test checks.

## Errors an agent cannot act on

- `orchestration_error` is raised across `apps/server/src/mcp`, for example in apps/server/src/mcp/HostStatusMcpService.ts, apps/server/src/mcp/HostThreadsMcpService.ts, apps/server/src/mcp/LaunchWatchService.ts, apps/server/src/mcp/OrchestratorMcpService.ts. The code does not say whether to retry, fix the input, or ask the user.
- `invalid_request` is raised across `apps/server/src/mcp`, for example in apps/server/src/mcp/HostStatusMcpService.ts, apps/server/src/mcp/HostThreadsMcpService.ts, apps/server/src/mcp/LaunchWatchService.ts, apps/server/src/mcp/McpHttpServer.ts. The code does not say whether to retry, fix the input, or ask the user.
- `OrchestratorMcpFailure` has only `code` and `message` (packages/contracts/src/orchestratorMcpFailure.ts `OrchestratorMcpFailure`): no retry hint, offending field, or next action. Recovery advice, where it exists, lives in message text.

## Where a human is required

These are the steps GOAT cannot finish without a person today, and how an agent finds out:

| Step                                          | How it surfaces to an agent                                                                                                                                                       | Evidence                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter a secret (webhook signing, credentials) | Agent calls `request_secret`; the user types the value in the app; the agent gets a `secretRef`. Only callable from inside a GOAT thread.                                         | packages/contracts/src/agentSurface/entries/handoff.ts, apps/server/src/mcp/completionWebhook.ts                 |
| Answer a provider question or approval        | The thread turns waiting; `goat_pending_request_list`, `goat_pending_request_read`, and `goat_pending_request_respond` let an agent answer, and escalation names the tool to use. | apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/QuestionEscalationService.ts, apps/server/src/mcp/PendingQuestionsMcpService.ts |
| Raise runtime or interaction mode             | The call fails with `runtime_mode_escalation_denied` or `interaction_mode_escalation_denied`. No tool requests approval, so the agent must stop and tell the user.                | packages/contracts/src/orchestratorMcpFailure.ts                                                                 |
| Grant a capability or credential              | The call fails with `capability_denied` or `thread_credential_required`; the user resolves it in settings or by issuing a token.                                                  | packages/contracts/src/orchestratorMcpFailure.ts                                                                 |
| T3 Connect sign-in (OAuth or device code)     | CLI only: `goat connect login`, or `--headless` for the device flow. No MCP tool starts it or reports its state.                                                                  | apps/server/src/cli/connect.ts                                                                                   |
| Pair a client                                 | `goat pair` or `goat auth pairing create` on the host, or Settings → Connections. No MCP tool.                                                                                    | apps/server/src/cli/pair.ts                                                                                      |
| Add an SSH host                               | `goat_connection_add_ssh` exists; host key trust, passphrases, and MFA prompts are not modelled as a handoff.                                                                     | packages/contracts/src/agentSurface/entries/connection.ts                                                        |
| Put `goat` on PATH                            | A desktop install writes a launcher under the GOAT home, off PATH; adding it to PATH is an opt-in desktop action.                                                                 | (not found), (not found)                                                                                         |

Tools whose description or schema tells the agent to involve the user: `create_threads` (user approval), `delegate_task` (user approval), `goat_cloud_launch` (user approval), `goat_computer_use_request` (user approval), `goat_connection_add_ssh` (user approval), `goat_decision_answer` (user approval), `goat_decision_get` (user approval, user answers a question), `goat_decision_list` (user approval), `goat_goal_apply` (user approval), `goat_goatclaw_sync` (user approval), `goat_host_link_create` (user approval, pairing), `goat_hub_device_join` (user approval), `goat_hub_device_leave` (user approval), `goat_hub_device_repair` (user approval), `goat_origin_reports_wait` (user approval), `goat_pending_request_list` (user approval), `goat_pending_request_respond` (user approval), `goat_provider_addable_list` (sign-in), `goat_provider_diagnose` (sign-in), `goat_provider_home_request` (user approval), `goat_provider_host_matrix` (sign-in), `goat_provider_link` (sign-in), `goat_provider_login_cancel` (sign-in), `goat_provider_login_start` (sign-in), `goat_provider_login_status` (sign-in), `goat_provider_setup_open` (user approval, sign-in), `goat_provider_sync` (user approval, sign-in), `goat_provider_sync_status` (user approval, sign-in), `goat_provider_update` (sign-in), `goat_ssh_host_add` (user approval), `goat_ssh_host_list` (sign-in), `goat_ssh_runtime_update` (user approval), `goat_ssh_thread_handoff` (user approval), `goat_ssh_thread_launch` (secret entry, user approval, user chooses in UI), `goat_storage_clean` (user approval), `goat_thread_checkpoint_restore` (user approval), `goat_thread_launch` (secret entry, user approval, user chooses in UI), `goat_thread_send` (user approval), `goat_thread_wait` (user answers a question), `request_secret` (secret entry), `schedule_task` (secret entry, user chooses in UI), `update_scheduled_task` (secret entry).

There is no single handoff primitive. Each case has its own tool, error code, or CLI step, and none returns a resumable handle the agent can wait on.

## CLI

The CLI operates a server; it is not an agent interface. Its 60 listed commands cover serving, auth tokens, pairing, the background service, updates, themes, traces, triage, and T3 Connect. Nothing lists, reads, or drives threads or tasks, and projects only have `goat project add`, `remove`, and `rename`. The one generic bridge, `goat acp-mcp-call`, is unlisted and its arguments are undescribed (apps/server/src/cli/acpMcpBridge.ts).

- 0 of 79 commands define usage examples, so `--help` never shows a worked call.
- 11 of 46 listed leaf commands offer `--json`: `goat auth pairing create`, `goat auth pairing list`, `goat auth session issue`, `goat auth session list`, `goat auth client create`, `goat auth client list`, `goat provider diagnose`, `goat thread list`, `goat thread start`, `goat thread send`, `goat thread show`.
- 20 commands have no description, all of them unlisted internals. Undescribed parameters: `goat acp-mcp-call arguments`, `goat call arguments`, `goat describe arguments`, `goat imessage enable --allow`, `goat imessage enable --own`, `goat imessage enable --full-access`, and 50 more.
- `goat auth client revoke` reuses the session revoke command under a second parent, so its help reads "Revoke an active session." (apps/server/src/cli/auth.ts).
- Server flags such as `--dev-url` repeat on subcommands that start no server, such as `goat auth pairing create`.

## Drift between docs and the registry

Scanned the Markdown docs (docs, structure, skills, root guides) and the agent prompt sources in `packages/provider-core/src/server`.

Names that look like tools but are not in the registry:

| Name           | Where                                                   |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `goat_eval`    | docs/internals/agent-surface.md                         |
| `list_changed` | docs/internals/agent-surface.md                         |
| `run_steps`    | structure/decisions/ADR-0022-cua-driver-computer-use.md |
| `run_script`   | structure/decisions/ADR-0022-cua-driver-computer-use.md |
| `list_apps`    | structure/decisions/ADR-0022-cua-driver-computer-use.md |

CLI invocations in the docs that do not resolve:

| Text                               | Problem                                    | Where                                                   |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `goat service install --no-start`  | `goat service install` has no `--no-start` | docs/user/background-service.md                         |
| `goat thread read -f threadId=$id` | no subcommand `read` under `goat thread`   | docs/user/outside-agents.md                             |
| `goat cua-lease-proxy --control`   | `goat` has no `--control`                  | structure/decisions/ADR-0022-cua-driver-computer-use.md |

100 of 202 tools are never named in any Markdown doc, and 95 are named in neither docs nor agent prompts: `channel_bot_home`, `channel_ingest`, `channel_task_export`, `channel_task_list`, `channel_task_move`, `channel_task_report`, `delete_scheduled_task`, `goat_attachment_discard`, `goat_attachment_pending_list`, `goat_attachment_prepare_upload`, `goat_cloud_machine_create`, `goat_cloud_machine_resume`, `goat_cloud_run_list`, `goat_connection_list`, `goat_connection_remove`, `goat_decision_list`, `goat_environment_preferences_update`, `goat_environment_read`, `goat_host_link_create`, `goat_host_link_list`, `goat_host_link_remove`, `goat_html_list`, `goat_hub_device_join`, `goat_hub_device_leave`, and 71 more. Agents learn these only from the MCP catalog.

Listed CLI commands no doc invokes: `goat auth pairing list`, `goat auth pairing revoke`, `goat project add`, `goat project remove`, `goat project rename`, `goat thread start`.

The server's `/llms.txt` lists every registry path with its summary, but arguments and examples are still served only by the MCP catalog.

## Fixes ranked by agent impact

1. **One error envelope with a machine code and a next action.** 7 error families and two failure modes (161 `return`, 41 `error`) all arrive as JSON inside text. Return `structuredContent` shaped like `{code, message, retryable, field?, next?}` from every tool so an agent branches on data.
2. **A single human handoff primitive.** Secrets, approvals, mode escalation, capability grants, and sign-in each surface differently (see "Where a human is required"). One handoff result with an id, what the user must do and where, plus one wait call, lets any agent pause and resume instead of failing.
3. **Serve the full tool reference from the registry.** 95 tools appear in no doc or prompt. `/llms.txt` now lists every path for the calling credential; `goat_describe` should serve arguments and examples from the same registry, with no committed reference pages (decision D14 in agent-surface.md).
4. **Describe every parameter.** 606 of 768 parameters have no description, and 137 tools describe none. Extend the catalog test at apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/core.test.ts `publishes unique tool names` to fail on an undescribed field.
5. **Publish the real argument contract.** 182 schemas advertise `additionalProperties: true` while the server refuses extra keys. Emit `false` so schema-validating clients reject a bad call before sending it.
6. **Retry keys on every mutating tool.** 81 mutating tools take no `clientRequestId`, so a dropped response leaves an agent unable to retry safely. Start with destructive tools and thread launch.
7. **One naming grammar.** Pick one shape for all 202 tools, keep old names as hidden aliases for a release, and drop the partial `goat_` prefix that the MCP server name already supplies.
8. **Derive hints from enforcement.** Compute `readOnlyHint` from the handler's `McpToolAccess` declaration instead of annotating it separately. 1 tools disagree or under-declare today, which misleads clients that auto-approve reads.
9. **Ship `goat` on PATH with the app.** Agents outside GOAT need a stable entry point. Put the launcher on PATH by default with a clear opt-out, and make `goat --version` the first-run check.
10. **Give the CLI an agent face.** Add listed `goat tool list` and `goat tool call <name> --json` generated from the same registry, so shells and CI reach every MCP capability through one documented grammar. Today only the unlisted `acp-mcp-call` exists.
11. **`--json` on every listed leaf command.** Only 11 of 46 offer it; agents parse human tables otherwise.
12. **Examples in help and tool descriptions, executed in tests.** 0 CLI commands use `Command.withExamples` and 3 tool descriptions show a call. Keep examples as data, render them into help and docs, and run them in a smoke test so they cannot rot.
13. **Uniform pagination.** Use one cursor shape everywhere and add it to list tools that lack one (`device_list`, `goat_attachment_pending_list`, `goat_cloud_machine_list`, `goat_connection_list`, `goat_host_link_list`, `goat_note_list`, `goat_pending_request_list`, `goat_provider_addable_list`, `goat_ssh_host_list`, `goat_thread_watch_list`, `list_scheduled_tasks`, `list_thread_pull_requests`).
14. **Move routing policy out of tool descriptions.** The longest description is 399 characters, mostly when-to-use guidance. Keep descriptions to what the tool does and its contract, and put policy in the orchestration prompt once.
15. **Group tools by resource.** Move queue and pending request tools out of the thread toolkit and thread launch out of the project toolkit, and give scheduled tasks one toolkit, so permissions, docs, and discovery follow the resource an agent is working on.
